I typed this in a while ago, but I'm fumble fingered and accidentally deleted 98 percent of my post, so here goes again:

The site is located in The Netherlands. This is a software-defined receiver. To put it in perspective, your car radio receives AM signals from about 540 to 1710 kilohertz. This radio receives from about 90 to 30,000 kilohertz (many many more frequencies).

To begin with, type "1053" into the frequency box. This is the same as tuning your car radio to 1053 on your AM dial. What you hear is an English-language broadcast being picked up in Norway. Probably some British pop radio station.

Looking over on the right side of the screen, click on the "Band" button. That will show only the AM broadcast band. See all the yellow lines moving vertically (the "waterfall")? Those are AM broadcast signals all being picked up at once. You are listening to the one frequency the arrow is pointing at.

Back to the left side, there are two buttons: --- and +++. Use those to change stations.

Once you have gotten bored with the AM band, go to the right side of the screen and click on "zoom out" a few times. Lower down in the band are some longwave stations and higher up will be some other shortwave stations; if you click in the black zone under the "waterfall" it will put you on a different frequency. Click on "band" to get the display into the general area, and use the plus and minus keys again to change frequencies.

There are a lot more options, but those should get you entertained for a good while.
